key_insight: Tuning BaTiO3 nanoparticle size and tetragonal distortion boosts Ti–O covalency, polarization, and piezoelectric output, enabling stronger lead-free hybrid nanogenerators.
engineering_relevance: This provides a scalable materials-design route for high-output, lead-free piezoelectric nanogenerators for self-powered electronics.
method: Ligand-assisted sol-gel synthesis of BaTiO3 nanoparticles
Annealing to compare BTO-900 (~54 nm) vs BTO-1200 (~104 nm)
XRD, Raman, PDF, and DFT used to link structure, bonding, and device performance
evidence_signal: The abstract reports ~100 V open-circuit voltage and ~29 μJ stored energy for BTO-900, while BTO-1200 achieved ~649 μW cm-2 power density and ~181 μA short-circuit current.
watch_item: Device output depends on annealing, particle size, and interfacial charge trapping, so performance may be sensitive to fabrication consistency and operating conditions.
paper_title: Small Distortions, Big Polarization: Tetragonal BaTiO3 Nanoparticles for High-Performance Piezoelectric Nanogenerators
